title: Morpheus v0.2: an anatomical compiler, a three-rule test of authorship, and audited self-improvement with room to improve
status: Committed before any confirmatory v0.2 run. v0.1 (prereg/PREREGISTRATION.json) is unchanged and its results stand.
disclosed_pilots: Compiler feasibility pilots used rules A and B on TRAINING tissues only (tail wounds from design seeds, fire-mask seed 4242, wound seed 999, 16 tissues), never the held-out H5 suite (seed 5). They motivated two protocol choices fixed below: voltage clamp rather than additive injection (rule A's body voltage sits at the +4 clip, so additive injection loses its gradient), and 12 clamp steps rather than 48 (48 optimised worse). Pilot numbers: posterior head index about -1.00 untreated, -0.73 to -0.77 designed, -0.92 to -0.96 shuffled.

rules.C: weights/rule_c.json: new, seed 2, same recipe as A and B (3000 iterations with the persistence phase). Trained after this file is committed.
rules.early: weights/rule_early.json: new, seed 3, same recipe but stopped at 300 iterations, so real improvements remain available to a self-improvement loop.

H5.claim: Anatomical compiler: a voltage pattern designed by gradient descent (per-grid-position clamp values, bounded to +-4, held for the first 12 steps after a tail amputation, optimised for 600 iterations of 16 training tissues towards a two-headed body) makes held-out tail stumps grow more head tissue where the tail was than the same clamp values spatially shuffled within the body.
H5.measure: posterior head index at the end of regeneration: in the normal body's tail region, fraction of alive cells typed head minus fraction typed tail
H5.test: one-sided sign-flip permutation on designed minus shuffled, alpha 0.05, bootstrap CI
H5.rules: designed separately for rule A (primary) and rule B (replication), design seed 0
H5.support_rule: p < 0.05 and CI lower bound > 0; 'replicated' if also so for rule B
H5.secondary: designed minus untreated (one-sided); fraction of tissues whose posterior head index is > 0 (a majority-head posterior), descriptive

H6.claim: Compiled memory: after regeneration under the designed clamp, a second tail amputation with no intervention still regrows more head tissue posteriorly than untreated tissues do.
H6.measure: posterior head index after the second regeneration (48 steps)
H6.test: one-sided sign-flip on designed-history minus untreated, alpha 0.05
H6.support_rule: p < 0.05 and CI lower bound > 0; rule A primary, rule B replication

H1C.claim: Authorship across rules (tie-break of v0.1's open H1): combining the one-sided p-values of rules A, B and C (the v0.1 H1 protocol, n 128, suite seed 1 for rule C), transplanted error streams impair regeneration.
H1C.test: Stouffer combination with equal weights of the three per-rule one-sided p-values, alpha 0.05
H1C.decision: 'supported' if pooled p < 0.05 and at least 2 of 3 rules individually p < 0.05; 'not supported' if pooled p >= 0.05; otherwise 'mixed'
H1C.also: rule C gets the full v0.1 battery (H1-H3, calibration) as a second replication of H2 and H3

H4b.claim: Starting from an under-trained rule (rule early), naive self-improvement loops overstate their progress more than audited loops (the v0.1 H4 hypothesis, now with genuine improvements available and more seeds).
H4b.design: 10 loop seeds x 30 proposals, same proposer and gate as v0.1
H4b.test: one-sided exact sign-flip on naive minus gated self-deception, alpha 0.05
H4b.secondary: gated true gain > 0 (one-sided sign-flip over seeds): does the audited loop still improve?; false-adoption fractions, descriptive

exploratory: cross-rule transfer: rule A's designed pattern applied to rule B and vice versa (does a bioelectric code transfer between rules that evolved opposite voltage signs?)
